title: College Football Live Updates: Week 12 Scores & Schedule – Ohio State, BYU, Wake Forest on CBS Sports
body:
The weekend’s slate of College Football Week 12 matchups delivered a mix of high‑stakes drama and surprising twists, leaving the College Football Playoff picture still in flux with just two weeks left in the regular season. Ohio State’s clash with a surging BYU squad, Wake Forest’s bid to cement its ACC resurgence, and several other marquee games produced a cascade of live updates, shifting rankings and new storylines that will shape the final stretch of the campaign.

Ohio State entered Saturday as the top‑ranked team in the nation, but the Buckeyes’ performance against BYU exposed vulnerabilities that could jeopardize their path to the playoff. After a tentative start, Ohio State’s offense found rhythm in the second half, ultimately pulling ahead with a 38‑31 victory. Quarterback C.J. Stroud threw for 315 yards and three touchdowns, while running back Miyan Williams added a crucial 78‑yard rushing display. Yet, the Buckeyes’ defense surrendered 421 total yards, allowing BYU to remain within striking distance for most of the game. The win keeps Ohio State at No. 1 in the polls, but the narrow margin and defensive lapses have sparked debate among analysts about the team’s resilience against elite competition.

Across the country, BYU proved why it remains a perennial giant‑killer. The Cougars, led by quarterback Jaren Hall, amassed 458 total yards and held a 31‑24 lead deep into the fourth quarter before the Buckeyes’ comeback. Hall’s poise under pressure, highlighted by a 45‑yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Isaiah Johnson, underscored BYU’s ability to compete at the highest level despite not being in a Power Five conference. The loss, while disappointing, bolstered BYU’s résumé and kept the program in the conversation for a potential at‑large playoff berth, especially if it can secure a victory in its final regular‑season game.

In the ACC, Wake Forest continued its upward trajectory with a decisive 45‑20 triumph over a struggling Virginia Tech side. The Demon Deacons’ balanced attack, featuring quarterback Sam Hartman’s 280 passing yards and running back Tyreke Smith’s 112 rushing yards, highlighted the team’s offensive versatility. Wake Forest’s defense forced three turnovers, showcasing a unit that has steadily improved since the season’s midpoint. The win propels the Demon Deacons into the top‑10 and solidifies their claim for a New Year’s Six bowl invitation, while also positioning them as a dark horse for the conference championship if they can maintain momentum against Florida State next week.

Other notable outcomes added layers to the playoff puzzle. Texas, ranked fourth, fell 31‑27 to Oklahoma State in a tightly contested battle, dropping the Longhorns to No. 6 and opening a window for Texas A&M and Clemson to climb. Meanwhile, Michigan, still perched at No. 3, secured a comfortable 38‑14 victory over Illinois, reinforcing its status as a playoff contender. The Big Ten’s internal hierarchy remains fluid, with Michigan, Ohio State and Iowa all jockeying for the coveted conference crown and the associated automatic playoff berth.

The Week 12 results have left the playoff landscape more intricate than ever. Ohio State’s narrow win keeps them atop the rankings, but the defensive concerns raised by the BYU game could prove costly if they face a high‑powered offense in the final weeks. BYU’s strong showing, coupled with a favorable remaining schedule, may earn the Cougars an at‑large spot if they finish the season undefeated. In the ACC, Wake Forest’s surge challenges the traditional power balance, while the Big Ten continues its internal scramble after Texas’ stumble.

Looking ahead, the final two weeks will be decisive. Ohio State must tighten its defense before the showdown with Michigan State, a game that could determine whether the Buckeyes retain the top seed. BYU’s next opponent, a ranked Mountain West team, will test the Cougars’ consistency and could cement their playoff aspirations. Wake Forest’s upcoming clash with Florida State will likely decide the ACC’s championship fate, and the Big Ten’s remaining contests will finalize the conference’s representation in the postseason. As the regular season races toward its conclusion, every play, every turnover and every late‑game decision will echo in the final rankings, shaping the narrative of college football’s most coveted prize.
